body_markdown:
What has thrills, chills, and something for every book lover? It’s the wonderfully wicked world of horror audiobooks.


With spooky season underway, we asked Spotify’s


**Katie del Rosario** , Associate Director, Audiobooks Editorial, and


**Lena Yang** , Senior Editor, Audiobooks, to walk us through some of the scariest stuff on Spotify. Whether you’re new to the genre or a longtime fan looking for something unexpected, our editors have put together a curated collection of some of horror’s most captivating tales.


“The genre is often associated with fear and violence, but at the core of so many great horror stories is some fundamental truth about what it means to be human,” Lena said. “The darkest books can often be strangely comforting as they give shape to our fears and, crucially, also show us someone trying to survive them.”


And there’s something special about


*listening* to these works. “Horror is inherently visceral, and audiobooks give you that immersive sensory experience with their sound designs,” Lena continued. “But the icing on the cake is hearing a narrator completely let loose, because horror gives them permission to perform at an intensity that other genres rarely call for. I’m talking creepy character voices and full-on shrieking—the more unhinged, the better.”


Read on…if you dare.


###


Ready to take your first steps into the dark depths of horror? These essential audiobooks offer the perfect entry point into horror to kick off your journey.


“We wanted to showcase just how much range exists within horror,” said Lena. “Our starter pack picks span generations and feature some of the genre’s most enduring themes while introducing many of the authors and stories that have helped define horror today. We know everyone’s threshold for fear is different, so these books range from creeping unease to all-out terror. Start with whatever feels most familiar and go from there!”


### ***Bird Box***


By Josh Malerman
Narrated by Cassandra Campbell


[Bird Box](https://open.spotify.com/show/0KWHW25i7N4z6Yjdv1uKLd) builds its terror entirely around what you can’t see. Creatures appear that drive anyone who looks at them to madness, and to survive in this world means keeping your eyes covered or shut. It’s a book that drives home how the fear of the unknown is more powerful than the thing itself.
—Katie


### ***The Lottery, and Seven Other Stories***


By Shirley Jackson
Narrated by Carol Jordan Stewart


While horror often contends with supernatural entities and beastly thrills, **Shirley Jackson** is interested in something closer to home: the darkness lurking in ordinary people.[The Lottery](https://open.spotify.com/show/5uPp8GH7xagfeW5L3K2Eqc) is this collection’s most enduring of Jackson’s short stories, but don’t skip the rest—they’re just as unnerving.
—Lena


### ***Mexican Gothic***


By Silvia Moreno-Garcia
Narrated by Frankie Corzo


[Mexican Gothic](https://open.spotify.com/show/42XET6uH4dKRxc1Hc1TSCW) , one of the defining gothic novels of this decade, delivers all the hallmarks of the genre. It’s the perfect place to start if your ideal horror vibe is less grotesque and more creeping, atmospheric dread, with a possibly haunted house on the side.
—Lena


### ***Rosemary’s Baby***


By Ira Levin
Narrated by Mia Farrow


This slow-burn masterpiece is paranoia horror at its most suffocating.[Rosemary’s Baby](https://open.spotify.com/show/26DQcU0J7rLcVfITtZIs5X) follows a woman who suspects her neighbors, husband, and own body are betraying her. **Mia Farrow** , who played Rosemary in the film, narrates this edition, making it something special.
—Katie


### ***It***


By Stephen King
Narrated by Steven Weber


A horror starter pack wouldn’t be complete without **Stephen King** ’s classic about how childhood fear lives inside you after you’ve grown up, and what it costs to go back and face it.[It](https://open.spotify.com/show/587ehiVcGuXjxKMECQneQ6) features one of the genre’s great ensembles, and the dual timeline is King’s writing at his best.
—Katie


### ***How to Sell a Haunted House***


By Grady Hendrix
Narrated by Jay Aaseng and Mikhaila Aaseng


Camp and horror have always made excellent bedfellows, and few contemporary writers understand that better than **Grady Hendrix** . Equal parts funny, frightening, and heartfelt,[How to Sell a Haunted House](https://open.spotify.com/show/6ag5Es2QFseoj0jJkCb4q8) is proof that horror doesn’t have to be bleak to get under your skin.
—Lena


###


If you’re ready to venture further into the shadows, Katie and Lena have plenty for you.


“Once you’ve read horror’s greatest hits, there’s a particular thrill in finding a book that can still surprise you,” said Lena. “These books take recognizable horror traditions and push them somewhere deeper, using ghosts, haunted houses, cosmic terrors, and the human body itself to explore ideas that can be difficult to put into words.”


### *The Fisherman*


By John Langan
Narrated by Danny Campbell


[The Fisherman](https://open.spotify.com/show/6yrnBgxH0fq7WullRNjrQG) is a modern classic in every sense, turning the incomprehensible scale of cosmic horror inward to make grief itself feel enormous and unknowable. Challenging, strange, and filled with chilling imagery, it’s a testament to the emotional depths horror can reach.
—Lena


### *The Lamb*


By Lucy Rose
Narrated by Emma Rydal


What do you owe the person who taught you how to be a monster? This dark debut is perhaps most unsettling because the horror is entirely intertwined with themes of motherhood, love, loyalty, and survival—oh, and cannibalism.
—Katie


### *The Eyes Are the Best Part*


By Monika Kim
Narrated by Jaine Ye


**Monika Kim** wraps female rage, immigrant family dynamics, and body horror together into something that is really uncomfortable but completely impossible to put down. You’ll feel a little unhinged reading it, but in the best way.
—Katie


### *A Haunting on the Hill*


By Elizabeth Hand
Narrated by Carol Monda


**Elizabeth Hand** takes us back to Shirley Jackson’s infamous Hill House in its first-ever authorized sequel.[A Haunting on the Hill](https://open.spotify.com/show/7oA8EPnNfXTWUJvO3wHVGK) is set in one of horror’s most enduring locations, complete with spooky sound design that had me turning around mid-dog walk in fright (and promptly feeling embarrassed).
—Lena


### *The Reformatory*


By Tananarive Due
Narrated by Joniece Abbott-Pratt


Set in 1950s Jim Crow-era Florida, **Tananarive Due** layers supernatural horror directly onto historical terror. In this book, the scariest thing isn’t the ghosts, but the humans running the school where the story takes place. It’s scary, devastating, and an essential listen.
—Katie


### *My Heart Is a Chainsaw*


By Stephen Graham Jones
Narrated by Cara Gee


To fully appreciate[My Heart Is a Chainsaw](https://open.spotify.com/show/7JWcTWf01Nwjwh9NDYjKd1?si=fbfecb936c2b4b69) , it helps to speak fluent slasher. We follow Jade Daniels, a horror film aficionado who is both thrilled and terrified to find herself living inside one. **Stephen Graham Jones** ’ blood-soaked love letter to slashers celebrates the genre while gleefully tearing into its conventions.
—Lena


###


Sure, they’re resident experts on everything eerie, but Katie and Lena are fans, too. Here are the audiobooks that top their list.


### *Bat Eater and Other Names for Cora Zeng*


By Kylie Lee Baker
Narrated by Natalie Naudus


Set amid the eerie emptiness and paranoia of COVID-era Manhattan, **Kylie Lee Baker** transforms trauma and anti-Asian hate into visceral supernatural horror that’s part ghost story, part serial killer thriller.[Bat Eater](https://open.spotify.com/show/4pQ6E64RpwUI4GnXTpw4b6) is incisive social commentary rendered grotesque in the best way.
—Lena


### *Pet Sematary*


By Stephen King
Narrated by Michael C. Hall


[Pet Sematary](https://open.spotify.com/show/3o1NhAHVPzqcgWbJACEU9J) is **Stephen King** at his most emotionally devastating. **Michael C. Hall** (of *Dexter* fame) is perfectly cast as the narrator—performing with a quiet menace in his voice that makes the dread build even more slowly than it would on the page.
—Katie


*Check out the*[Horror Fiction audiobook hub](https://open.spotify.com/genre/0JQ5DAqbMKFEyUVaPmCls6) *on Spotify for even more spine-tingling tales, and stay tuned for more genre deep dives coming soon.*
